Cargo and freight agents arrange the movement of incoming and outgoing cargo, with outputs including quotations and shipping arrangements, documents, and milestone records; some positions also take part in cargo tallies, securing, or loading and unloading. O*NET currently places this at Job Zone 1–2, with interest code CE and a Bright Outlook designation. First verify the target position's duties, jurisdiction, and authorization, then decide on investment.

Low-cost trial: using the three fictional shipments from the T1 pathway and the R/S rules, calculate charges and verify time limits and capability, handle the three differences in piece count / temperature control / attributes and a delay injection, and submit four deliverables: quotation, differences, exceptions, and review. Pen and paper are enough, with no connection to real systems; self-check against the reference and observe whether you want to keep exploring.

Signals to keep exploring: willingness to re-verify weight, rates, deadlines, and fields repeatedly, the ability to keep a pending-verification status when attributes or authorization have not been checked, and acceptance of review and changes. Use T1 to observe how the tasks feel; completing them does not mean you are competent or qualified.

Education, certification, and authorization are verified separately. O*NET Job Zone 1–2; the new-hire education judgments are 31% bachelor's, 19% some college no degree, and 18% postsecondary certificate, which is not the actual composition of practitioners. For this occupation BLS gives typical entry with a high school diploma or equivalent, no related work experience, and short-term on-the-job training, which is a U.S. overview. The certification entry lists 6 items and is only a discovery list. In the United States, acting as a customs broker for others in customs business in principle requires a license; the CBP 2025 guidance also lists exceptions such as importers and exporters handling only their own business and their authorized regular employees, and qualifying broker employees. In China, the information filing of international freight forwarding enterprises and their branches is an institutional matter, not an individual customs declaration certificate. China's 2024 civil aviation dangerous goods rules require relevant practitioners to be trained and pass assessment, and a shipper's agent must hold a shipper's authorization letter; carrier permits, training, and individual position authorization are verified separately.

This occupation arranges cargo transport and maintains quotations, documents, milestones, and difference records, and may choose transport modes or take part in on-site operations according to duties and authorization. Position records cannot by themselves prove a customs broker license, dangerous goods training, a carrier permit, or final claims liability; for China only the industry proxy is retained.

The work of this occupation falls into three categories: first, orders and solutions (taking orders and inquiries, comparing carrier capability and rates, advising clients on transport and payment methods, and recording freight charges and weight and quoting); second, documents and compliance (determining the transport mode and preparing bills of lading and invoices and other transport documents, checking import and export documents and classifying goods with tariff codes, arranging cargo insurance, and handling dangerous goods documentation boundaries as required); third, milestones and exceptions (tracking delivery progress, notifying consignees and arranging delivery, picking up and tracing cargo, resolving transport problems with suppliers or the claims department, and checking and tallying received goods and recording shortages and rejected damaged goods). All three share the same chain centered on document consistency, visible milestones, and escalatable exceptions.
Orders and solutions

Take the order and confirm the goods and deadline and service requirements → compare carrier capability and rates and give a solution and quotation → arrange pickup and deliver the goods to the loading platform → confirm booking and stowage → record freight charges and weight and agreed conditions → form a written confirmation
Documents and compliance

Determine the transport mode and shipping terms → prepare bills of lading and invoices and other transport documents → check import and export documents and classify the goods → arrange cargo insurance and check the coverage → re-verify weight and piece count and rates and taxes and fees → file and retain and pass on documents as required

Track each milestone and record time and status → notify the consignee and arrange delivery → pick up or trace cargo that has not arrived → check and tally received goods against the documents → record shortages and rejected damaged goods and communicate handling → escalate delays and cargo damage and document differences to the client and carrier and the person authorized to handle them

What is compared here is the U.S. occupational task emphasis: this occupation arranges cargo movement and documents; managers coordinate transport and warehousing and personnel; purchasing agents manage procurement and may track deliveries; customs brokers focus on customs formalities; logisticians coordinate the product life cycle; logistics analysts analyze and may track cargo flows; and the freight forwarding subcategory studies rates and routes and arranges services. The tasks overlap, and qualifications and authorization are verified separately.
Core purpose

To complete the handover of one shipment under the agreed deadline and cost and compliance conditions: carrier solutions and quotations keep the conditions verifiable, document consistency and filing keep the process traceable, and milestone tracking and exception escalation keep problems from being delayed.
Main subjects and basis

The subjects are clients and consignees and their goods and deadline requirements, as well as carriers (airlines, railways, trucking and shipping companies) and cargo terminals and wharves and warehouse operators, customs brokers and insurers, and packing and loading personnel; the basis is transport contracts and shipping terms and rate tables, the rules for completing and reviewing bills of lading and invoices and other transport documents, import and export document and tariff classification requirements, the documentation and training rules for dangerous goods transport, the U.S. customs broker license requirement, mainland China's rules on international freight forwarding operations and on the transport of dangerous goods by civil aviation, and the institution's internal quotation and credit and exception escalation processes.
Core process

Take the order and confirm requirements, compare carrier solutions and quote, arrange pickup and booking and stowage, prepare and review transport documents, arrange insurance and check coverage, track milestones and notify for delivery, check and tally received goods against documents, and record shortages and rejections and escalate exceptions.
Main outputs

Inquiry and quotation records, booking and stowage plans, bills of lading and invoices and other transport documents, import and export document checks and tariff classification records, insurance arrangement records, milestone tracking and delivery notification records, receiving check and shortage and rejection records, exception and escalation and claims follow-up records, and the cargo movement ledger.
Accountable parties

Quotation, shipping arrangement, documentation, and milestone tasks are carried out according to the position's division of labor; freight agents may also lawfully choose the transport mode. The liability of carriers, shippers and their agents, customs business entities, and insurers is determined separately under the applicable law and contract, and authority is not inferred from the occupational title. In the United States, acting as a customs broker for others in customs business in principle requires a license; the CBP 2025 guidance also lists exceptions such as importers and exporters handling only their own business and their authorized regular employees, and qualifying broker employees. In China, the information filing of international freight forwarding enterprises and their branches is an institutional matter, not an individual customs declaration certificate. China's 2024 civil aviation dangerous goods rules require relevant practitioners to be trained and pass assessment, and a shipper's agent must hold a shipper's authorization letter; carrier permits, training, and individual position authorization are verified separately.
Authority and approval

Whether one may quote externally and commit to space and deadlines, prepare and sign bills of lading and other transport documents, handle import and export customs matters, accept dangerous goods, and how far one may handle cargo damage and claims is determined by the position's duties and institutional authorization, the transport contract and carrier agreement, and the statutory rules on customs declaration and dangerous goods and dangerous goods transport; authority comes from position authorization and qualification records and does not arise from work experience alone; when something is found to be beyond the authorized scope or documents do not match the actual goods, stop first and report.
Conclusion boundaries

Milestone records and document filing describe how this shipment was executed under the given transport conditions and within the authorized scope; they are not a final determination of liability, nor do they replace the judgments made by carriers and customs brokers and insurers under agreement and regulation, and they are updated as transport conditions and documents are supplemented; when citing, state the shipping terms, the document version, and the record period at the same time.

Before starting, verify at least six items: job duties (leaning toward orders and quotations, documents and compliance, milestones and exception handling, or warehousing and loading coordination), the scope of authority to commit externally (quotations, space, deadlines, claims), whether import and export customs declaration or dangerous goods acceptance is involved (and the corresponding qualification and training requirements), the systems and document platforms and data permissions used, shift and duty and overtime arrangements, and the exception and escalation and assessment methods.
Occupational framing

U.S. O*NET-SOC43-5011.00, in the office and administrative support category; the summary interest code is CE, and the detailed scores are conventional 89, enterprising 64, realistic 36. The specific interest fields office 56, accounting 30, and administrative management 28 cannot be treated as individual score thresholds from the ranking. Preparation level Job Zone1–2, SVP below 6; labeled Bright Outlook. The 2025 industry page shows 91% transportation and warehousing and 9% other, which is only a distribution. The Chinese name does not establish a Chinese occupational subcategory or a one-to-one wage mapping.
Education and training pathways

U.S. O*NET preparation level Job Zone1–2: usually a high school diploma or equivalent, and some occupations may not require it; the preparation and training range is a merged occupational group overview. For the specific SOC43-5011 BLS gives typical entry with a high school diploma or equivalent, no related experience, and short-term on-the-job training. O*NET's judgment on new-hire education is 31% bachelor's, 19% some college no degree, and 18% postsecondary certificate. Chinese recruitment and business authorization are verified separately, and the U.S. overview is not applied as a Chinese legal requirement.
Methods and tools

The O*NET technology list names 11 categories of software skills, and the Hot Technologies page shows 6 items (Microsoft Office 7%, Excel 6%, Outlook 4%, Word 2%, PowerPoint 1%, and SAP below 1%; the data source is 2025 U.S. job postings from Lightcast). The editorial suggestion is to verify whether the target position mainly uses transport management and booking and tracking systems, customs declaration and document filing platforms, document templates such as bills of lading and invoices and packing lists, rate and mileage and weight calculation tools, barcode scanning and warehouse management systems, and office and email and telephone communication tools.
Safety and work permits

The mix of office, cargo terminal, and on-site tasks is verified against the specific position; the task list cannot prove that every position frequently goes to the warehouse. O*NET work context shows: 61% having telephone conversations every day; 60% in continuous contact with others; 58% reporting a lot of freedom over tasks and priorities and goals; 54% considering accuracy very important; 52% keeping a slight close distance (such as in the same office) with others; 49% facing time pressure at least once a week but not every day; 49% considering dealing with external customers or the public extremely important; 49% having to deal with unpleasant or angry or discourteous people at least once a month but not every week; 47% considering working with a team extremely important; 43% considering decisions to have an important impact on colleagues or organizational outcomes; 43% considering the level of competition in the job very high; 37% having fairly high responsibility for the health and safety of other workers; 34% working 40 hours per week; 33% spending time continuously using hands to handle and control objects and tools; 30% reporting limited decision freedom; 28% making decisions at least once a week but not every day; 28% sitting about half the time; 16% never indoors in a controlled environment; 47% considering the consequences of error serious. Work requirements follow transport contracts and institutional safety procedures, and entering loading and warehouse areas requires complying with on-site safety requirements.
Training and regulatory requirements

In the United States, acting as a customs broker for others in customs business in principle requires a license; the CBP 2025 guidance also lists exceptions such as importers and exporters handling only their own business and their authorized regular employees, and qualifying broker employees. In China, the information filing of international freight forwarding enterprises and their branches is an institutional matter, not an individual customs declaration certificate. China's 2024 civil aviation dangerous goods rules require relevant practitioners to be trained and pass assessment, and a shipper's agent must hold a shipper's authorization letter; carrier permits, training, and individual position authorization are verified separately.
Pay and hours

The shift and office/on-site task mix is verified against the target employer; the O*NET work context shows 49% facing time pressure at least once a week but not every day, 34% working 40 hours per week, 43% considering the level of competition in the job very high, and 58% reporting a lot of freedom over tasks and priorities and goals. The U.S. 2025 BLS OEWS national wage framing (relayed via O*NET) is: median hourly wage 25.13 USD and median annual wage 52,260 USD; the annual wage 10th to 90th percentile is 38,340 to 79,810 USD; BLS projects 2025—2035 employment growth of 6.2%, a net increase of about 6,200 positions, and about 9,000 average annual job openings. For mainland China this evidence route only has industry-level proxy framing (2025 urban non-private units in transportation, warehousing and postal services average annual wage 133,981 yuan, and urban private units in the same category 73,133 yuan), neither of which is this occupation's exact framing, and this page marks this at each place. When comparing opportunities, include shifts and duty and overtime and commission and the scope of responsibility in a written agreement.

Cargo and freight agents (O*NET-SOC 43-5011.00, Cargo and Freight Agents) expedite and route the movement of incoming and outgoing cargo and freight shipments between airline, train, and trucking terminals and shipping docks: taking orders from customers, arranging pickup of freight and cargo for delivery to the loading platform, and preparing and examining bills of lading to determine shipping charges and tariffs. Daily work includes: negotiating and arranging cargo transport with shipping or freight companies; determining the transport mode and preparing bills of lading, invoices, and other transport documents; tracking cargo delivery progress; advising customers on transport and payment methods; estimating freight charges or postal rates and recording freight charges and weight; keeping records of all goods shipped, received, and stored; notifying consignees or passengers or customers of the arrival of cargo or baggage and arranging delivery; picking up stored goods and tracing lost goods when necessary; entering transport information into computers by hand or with handheld scanners; preparing manifests and declaring aircraft passenger and baggage and mail and cargo weights and transmitting the data to the destination; arranging insurance for cargo; installing straps and supports and dunnage on loads to prevent shifting or damage in transit; checking import and export documents to determine cargo contents and classifying goods by rate or tariff group using tariff code systems; coordinating and supervising workers engaged in packing and shipping; contacting suppliers or claims departments to resolve transport problems or contacting service stations to arrange repairs; checking and tallying received goods against invoices or other documents, recording shortages, and rejecting damaged goods; using forklifts and hand trucks and other equipment to move received goods to the nearest available flight or the appropriate storage area or department; directing trucks to loading doors or designated staging areas and assisting with safe loading and unloading; assembling containers and crates for shipping items such as machines or vehicles; maintaining inventory of packing materials; directing or participating in loading to ensure loads are complete and weight is evenly distributed; packing goods using tools such as staplers and strapping machines and hammers; affixing address labels and identification codes and shipping instructions on containers; and opening containers and unpacking goods with hand tools such as tin snips and pry bars. The tasks cover the occupational group, and not every position performs all of them every day; transport mode selection, signing, customs declaration, and dangerous goods activities must still be carried out under the applicable jurisdiction, training, and authorization.

O*NET occupational identity and tasks: O*NET-SOC 43-5011.00 Cargo and Freight Agents, on the page updated in 2026, listed as Job Zone 1–2 (little to some preparation, SVP below 6.0), with a Bright Outlook designation. The official duties are 'Expedite and route movement of incoming and outgoing cargo and freight shipments in airline, train, and trucking terminals and shipping docks. Take orders from customers and arrange pickup of freight and cargo for delivery to loading platform. Prepare and examine bills of lading to determine shipping charges and tariffs.'; the page lists 24 tasks (9 core + 15 supplementary), covering negotiating and arranging cargo transport with shipping or freight companies (72), determining the transport mode and preparing bills of lading and invoices and other transport documents (68), tracking cargo delivery progress (64), advising customers on transport and payment methods (62), estimating freight charges or postal rates and recording freight charges and weight (60), keeping records of goods shipped and received and stored (58), notifying consignees or customers of arrival and arranging delivery (58), picking up stored goods and tracing lost goods (52), entering transport information into computers by hand or scanner (51), and supplementary tasks such as preparing manifests and declaring weights (63), arranging insurance for cargo (61), installing straps and supports and dunnage (60), checking import and export documents and classifying goods with tariff codes (57), coordinating and supervising packing and shipping workers (56), contacting suppliers or claims departments to resolve transport problems (56), checking and tallying received goods against invoices and recording shortages (54), moving received goods to flights or storage areas (54), directing trucks to loading doors and assisting with safe loading and unloading (50), assembling containers and crates (49), maintaining packing material inventory (41), directing or participating in loading to ensure complete loads and even weight distribution (41), packing goods with tools (41), affixing address labels and identification codes and shipping instructions (39), and opening containers and unpacking goods (38).

U.S. 2025 OEWS national annual wage 10/25/50/75/90 percentiles are 38340/45710/52260/63390/79810 USD; the corresponding hourly wages are 18.43/21.98/25.13/30.48/38.37 USD. Percentiles are not an individual's starting pay or take-home income, and this round did not obtain the original average table, so an average cannot be inferred from the percentiles.

China 2025 transportation, warehousing and postal services averages: urban non-private 133981 and private 73133 yuan/year, which are only proxies for the whole industry, not this occupation's median or starting wage. This round did not establish a one-to-one Chinese subcategory mapping, nor did it verify the full text of the occupational code, so the closest entry is not used as an authoritative conclusion.

Industry distribution and employment background: the O*NET 2025 industry distribution shows 91% of this occupation in transportation and warehousing and 9% in other industries; the BLS Table 1.2 projection framing is about 100,300 in 2025, with 2025—2035 employment growth of 6.2%, a net increase of about 6,200 positions, and about 9,000 average annual job openings (including replacement needs such as turnover and retirement); position demand is affected by trade volume and freight structure, e-commerce and cross-border fulfillment, carrier capacity and freight rate volatility, the degree of automation and document digitization, and the supply of people with transport and documentation and compliance knowledge. The occupation is labeled Bright Outlook (good growth prospects), but among its O*NET related occupations, freight forwarders (43-5011.01), aircraft cargo handling supervisors (53-1041.00), and light truck drivers (53-3033.00) are also labeled Bright Outlook and are different occupational identities.

Tool signals and abilities: the technology list names 11 categories of software skills, and the Hot Technologies page shows 6 items (Microsoft Office 7%, Excel 6%, Outlook 4%, Word 2%, PowerPoint 1%, SAP below 1%); work activities center on getting information (78), recording information and decision making and problem solving (72 each), handling and moving objects (65), and communicating with people outside the organization and controlling machines and processes and judging the qualities of objects and services and monitoring processes and materials (61 each); basic skills center on oral expression (66) and active listening (63) and critical thinking and reading comprehension (56 each), with mathematics 31 and science 0; transferable skills center on negotiation and time management (53 each) and complex problem solving and coordination and service orientation and social perceptiveness (50 each); knowledge centers on transportation (89) and geography (88) and public safety and security (76) and English language (73) and administration and management (72); the interest code is CE (conventional, enterprising); the detailed page realistic score is 36 and cannot be added into the summary code; work styles center on dependability (88) and attention to detail (79) and integrity (58) and adaptability (47).

paragraphs: This page compares cargo and freight agents with six adjacent directions on the same set of dimensions: occupational direction, core work and outputs, key differences, and which direction each preference is a better fit for. Adjacent directions are described by their own official occupational descriptions and do not mean that job titles or qualifications and signing authority are interchangeable.

The comparison basis is the U.S. definitions and tasks of this occupation and the six adjacent O*NET occupations, which have been verified item by item this round. The tasks overlap, and the editorial selection advice is not a switching probability; the U.S. customs business exceptions and the Chinese enterprise filing and civil aviation dangerous goods training are verified separately.

The table below compares the differences in duties and outputs between cargo and freight agents and adjacent directions; the basis for judgment is the main outputs, what the work is accountable for, and the required qualifications, not how similar the job titles sound.
Overlaps with this occupation in on-site work and documents; the main difference is management and resource coordination responsibility.
If you are willing to manage people and budgets and operations, this direction can be compared further.
Coordinating transport and warehousing and personnel and budgets and operations; may also check invoices and manifests and negotiate freight rates.
Transportation, storage, and distribution managers
Purchasing focuses on what to buy, from whom, and the procurement contract; transport delivery is not entirely excluded.
If you are willing to study procurement terms and suppliers, this direction can be compared.
Purchasing the equipment, materials, or services needed, negotiating contracts, and evaluating suppliers; may track deliveries and arrange freight payment.
Purchasing agents
U.S. customs business on behalf of others has a licensing principle and statutory exceptions, and not all documentation staff must hold a personal license.
If you are willing to study customs business, the target jurisdiction's license and institutional permits and employee authorization can be verified.
Preparing customs documents and duties and taxes and client representation and authorized signing; may also coordinate transport and warehousing.
Customs brokers
The scope covers the life cycle and resources and project coordination, not just writing analysis reports; there may be execution overlap with this occupation.
If you are willing to coordinate resources and cross-departmental projects, logisticians can be compared.
Analyzing and coordinating product life cycle logistics from procurement and distribution and delivery to final disposition of resources.
Logisticians (13-1081.00)
Analysis methods and process improvement are the focus, but it cannot be said that they only touch models and never handle in-transit business at all.
If you are willing to use data to analyze processes and improve transport arrangements, logistics analysts can be compared.
Analyzing delivery and supply chain processes and maintaining models and performance data; may also manage invoices and track transport.
Logistics analysts (13-1081.02)
A more specific O*NET occupational profile within 43-5011 that overlaps heavily with the tasks on this page; Chinese enterprise filing separately falls under jurisdictional rules.
If you are willing to go deeper into route comparison and cross-border services, this subcategory can be compared, with the applicable institutional and individual requirements verified.
Studying rates and routes and transport modes and cross-border rules, and arranging transport and warehousing and inland services and documents.
Freight forwarders (43-5011.01)

Conclusion: the basis for choosing a direction is the main outputs, what the work is accountable for, and the required qualifications, not how similar the names sound; after deciding on a direction, verify item by item the target position's authorized scope (quotations and space commitments and claims), whether customs declaration or dangerous goods are involved and the corresponding license and training requirements, the systems and data permissions used, and shift and duty arrangements, and keep written confirmation.

paragraphs: Students or career changers preparing to enter this occupation

Start with one closed loop using self-made materials: for three fictional shipments (ordinary cargo, cargo needing temperature control or securing, and cargo containing dangerous goods components), write the inquiry and comparison and quotation, booking and stowage, the list of documents to be prepared, and the milestone tracking and exception escalation pathway, mark three possible documentation or compliance risks and two situations that must be escalated, then ask a peer to challenge you; at the same time verify the target position's authorized scope (quotations and space commitments and claims) and whether customs declaration or dangerous goods are involved.
Incumbent cargo and freight agents

Use tools in reviewable steps such as rate and mileage and weight retrieval and price comparison, first drafts of bills of lading and invoices and packing lists, milestone and ledger organizing, and client notification and communication text drafting; the final choice of transport mode and carrier, quotations and space commitments, judgments on import and export documents and tariff classification, identification of dangerous goods boundaries, and exception escalation must still be verified and documented by authorized personnel.
Institutional operations and compliance management positions

Before introducing automated price comparison, automated document preparation, milestone forecasting, or exception warning tools, first clarify the data sources and authorization, whether they comply with transport and customs and dangerous goods rules, who confirms the algorithmic suggestions, who is responsible for quotations and commitments and compliance conclusions, and ensure there is substantive human review and a paper trail before external commitments and document release.
Mentoring and business training

Focus training on transport modes and rate structures, document consistency and checking methods, reading import and export documents and tariff classification, boundary identification and escalation processes for dangerous goods and special cargo, and carrier and client communication and negotiation; also train the habit of staying cautious about automated price comparison and automated document results and going back to original documents and freight rates and the actual cargo state before confirming.

Insufficient evidence: this round obtained no measurement of this occupation's actual AI adoption rate, efficiency gain, or displacement rate. Retrieval, document first drafts, and ledger organizing can be trialed on fictional materials with errors and review costs checked; task exposure, actual adoption, and employment projections are different objects. All dates and rates and cargo are paper models, not real transport conditions. 2026-10-05 09:00 from the same fictional origin to destination: A ordinary paper boxes, 2 boxes totaling 80kg, 0.40m³, required before October 7 18:00; B temperature-controlled sample, 1 box, 30kg, 0.20m³, required before October 6 18:00 with full-journey 2–8°C temperature records; C sample labeled 'contains battery', 1 box, 20kg, 0.10m³, client requires arrival by October 6 but there is no composition / classification / test documentation.

Plan R: chargeable weight = max(actual weight kg, volume m³ × 200kg/m³), 4 yuan/kg + 100 yuan per shipment, arrival in 48 hours, ordinary cargo capability only, no temperature-controlled or battery cargo. Plan S: chargeable weight = max(actual weight kg, volume m³ × 250kg/m³), 8 yuan/kg + 150 yuan per shipment, arrival in 24 hours; B adds 80 yuan and 2–8°C and temperature records are already confirmed in writing; whether C is accepted is unconfirmed. Both models are calculated per the whole kilograms given, with no other taxes or fees.

Original instructions: A 2 boxes/80kg, B 1 box/30kg, C 1 box/20kg. Drafts: A invoice 2 boxes/80kg, packing list 3 boxes/80kg; B instructions require 2–8°C but the transport instruction says ambient temperature; C draft says ordinary cargo. Do not alter the originals to eliminate discrepancies.
Tasks and exception injection

Task 1: calculate the chargeable weight and total price for both plans A/B, and compare by deadline and cargo capability and confirmed conditions; for C only the model amount can be calculated and it cannot serve as an executable quotation. List the basis for the choice and the undecided conditions.

Task 2: compile a check table for instruction / invoice / packing list / transport instruction, find the three differences in A piece count, B temperature control, and C attributes, and note the pending checks and stop conditions. Task 3: inject that carrier R notifies at October 5 17:00 that A's estimated arrival is changed to October 8 09:00; mark that the original deadline is exceeded, the client has not agreed, and an alternative must be asked about, and it must not be written that the booking has been re-made.

Record columns: shipment number, original version, time, event, verified/unverified, temporary stop items, responsibility code, next verification action. Exception information goes to responsible person Q and client code K; these are fictional roles.
Reference calculation and handling

A: R chargeable 80kg, total 420 yuan, original estimate October 7 09:00 meets the deadline; S chargeable 100kg, total 950 yuan, October 6 09:00 meets it. Initially R is cheaper. B: R chargeable 40kg model 260 yuan, but it has no temperature control capability and 48 hours exceeds the deadline, so it is not selectable; S chargeable 50kg, total 630 yuan (400+150+80), October 6 09:00 with temperature control already confirmed, meeting the paper conditions.

C: R model 180 yuan, S model 350 yuan; neither can be a conclusion of acceptance or shippability. Record that the attributes are unverified, stop the current shipment confirmation, and have appropriate personnel verify classification, training, documents, and carrier acceptance by jurisdiction; a dangerous goods category or exemption must not be judged from 'contains battery' alone.

For A the piece count is based on the original instruction and cargo check as the pending basis, B's instruction is to be corrected and the temperature control confirmation re-verified, C's ordinary-cargo draft is pending, and signatures must not be fabricated. After the delay injection R no longer meets the deadline; S at this point has neither space nor a new quotation verified, so it can only be asked about and await client and authorized confirmation, and the initial S plan must not automatically be written as the actual replacement.

Deliver the quotation comparison table, the field difference table, the milestone exception record, and a one-page review. Self-check against the reference or ask someone to review, noting the actual method and change records, and it can be completed even with no one on duty. Suggested preparation and calculation 40 minutes, document checking 50 minutes, exceptions and review 30 minutes.

Do not handle real cargo, real booking/customs systems, or hazardous substances, and do not include real client data. Record A's October 5 17:00 delay notice, October 8 09:00 exceeding the deadline, and the new S quotation/space/client consent pending; it must not be falsely stated that the carrier has been changed.
